summary: Evaluation of 14 days of closed-loop telemetry from Nightscout (3,995 valid CGM entries, 98.7% coverage) indicates an 86.0% time in range, 8.9% time above range, and 5.1% time below range. The user operates AAPS with SMB and UAM enabled, dynamic ISF at 70%, and a flat ISF of 56 mg/dL/U. While overnight and fasting periods show strong stability with basal rates ranging from 0.5 to 0.8 U/h, afternoon glycemic excursions (peaks up to 293 mg/dL) occur alongside unannounced meal absorption. Hypoglycemia (<70 mg/dL) at 5.1% indicates that insulin delivery requires careful management. Because carbohydrate treatment entries are absent from the logs, keeping baseline profile parameters while transitioning toward consistent meal carbohydrate announcements is recommended.
issues: Postprandial and afternoon hyperglycemia peaks reaching up to 293 mg/dL due to unannounced or unmeasured carbohydrate intake.
Time below range of 5.1% (<70 mg/dL), indicating occasional over-delivery or stacking during fasting or post-peak windows.
Absence of logged carbohydrate treatment entries in Nightscout, requiring the closed-loop system to rely entirely on UAM detection.
education: Unannounced Meal (UAM) detection in AAPS identifies rising glucose trends and delivers microboluses automatically, but proactive meal announcements and prebolusing reduce peak postprandial heights.
Dynamic ISF adjusts sensitivity based on glucose momentum, tightening insulin delivery during sharp rises and relaxing it during drops to protect against hypoglycemia.
strengths: Excellent CGM data quality with 98.7% coverage over the 14-day evaluation period.
Strong overnight and fasting glucose stability, with time in range exceeding 85-98% during early morning hours.
Robust closed-loop automation utilizing SMB and UAM to effectively catch and manage unannounced glucose fluctuations.
safety_notes: This is decision-support content only. The user must independently verify every proposed change, make changes one at a time, and monitor glucose closely.
TuneMyBG prepares data for review only and does not provide medical advice.

analysis_steps.evidence: 3,995 valid CGM entries over 14 days with 98.7% coverage, 10 gaps (largest 65.0 minutes), 2,315 treatments, and 6,214 device statuses.
analysis_steps.findings: Dataset is highly reliable and continuous for closed-loop telemetry evaluation.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Zero carb treatment entries recorded in summary statistics.

analysis_steps.evidence: TIR 86.0%, TAR 8.9%, TBR 5.1%, CV 32.6%, glucose extremes ranging from 41 mg/dL to 293 mg/dL.
analysis_steps.findings: Hypoglycemia frequency (5.1%) crosses safety thresholds during late afternoon and overnight, while afternoon hyperglycemia spikes require careful handling.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Absence of explicit carbohydrate meal logs.

analysis_steps.evidence: Hourly local glucose profiles show strong overnight stability (00:00 local average 93.3 mg/dL) and afternoon elevations (15:00-16:00 local averages up to 162.8 mg/dL).
analysis_steps.findings: Overnight basal rates maintain stable fasting glucose, while afternoon elevations reflect unannounced meal impacts or increased insulin resistance.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Lack of meal entry tags prevents separation of basal drift from unannounced meal absorption.

analysis_steps.evidence: Active profile uses a flat ISF of 56 mg/dL/U, CR segments from 10.5 to 13.2 g/U, 10-hour DIA, and dynamic ISF adjustment factor of 70%.
analysis_steps.findings: Dynamic sensitivity scaling actively manages variability, but correction response windows show mixed performance due to unrecorded meals.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Zero logged carb entries restrict direct validation of carb ratio segments.

analysis_steps.findings: Automation settings are internally consistent and actively support unannounced glucose management.

analysis_steps.evidence: Autosens disabled (false), dynamic sensitivity enabled (true, 70%), max basal 12 U/h, max IOB 25 U.
analysis_steps.findings: Safety limits and dynamic sensitivity parameters provide appropriate headroom without excessive risk.

analysis_steps.evidence: Total carbs recorded as 0.0 g across treatments; therapy response windows show mixed post-correction outcomes.
analysis_steps.findings: System relies entirely on UAM and microboluses; recording carbohydrate entries will improve closed-loop precision.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Explicit meal carb data is missing from the telemetry log.

analysis_steps.evidence: min_5m_carbimpact set to 8 mg/dL/5 min and meal_max_absorption_hours set to 7 h.
analysis_steps.findings: Absorption parameters support UAM tracking; altering absorption duration is unsupported without meal logs.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Absence of meal composition and extended carb entries.

analysis_steps.evidence: Combined evaluation of 14 days of CGM data, closed-loop telemetry, safety metrics (5.1% TBR, 86% TIR), and active profile settings.
analysis_steps.findings: Keep current profile settings and automation configurations unchanged while initiating consistent meal carbohydrate logging to evaluate postprandial dynamics.

recommendations.title: Begin Consistent Carbohydrate Logging
recommendations.description: In the absence of logged carb entries, the closed-loop system relies entirely on UAM detection, contributing to postprandial afternoon peaks up to 293 mg/dL. Logging meals consistently will enable precise validation of carb ratios.

recommendations.title: Maintain Baseline Basal and ISF Settings
recommendations.description: Overnight stability is strong, but time below range (5.1%) counsels against altering basal or ISF parameters until meal logging provides clear postprandial data.

profile_recommendation.rationale: Overnight glucose control is stable (TIR >85-98% overnight), and hypoglycemia risk (5.1% <70 mg/dL) indicates that current basal rates and ISF should not be altered prematurely while carbohydrate entries are unrecorded.
profile_recommendation.next_check: Log carbohydrate entries for all meals over the next 7 days to evaluate postprandial absorption and validate profile carb ratios before considering parameter adjustments.
profile_recommendation.recommendation: Keep current profile settings and focus on consistent meal carbohydrate tracking.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Maintain smb_enabled=true and uam_enabled=true as the core automation engine. Transition toward recording carbohydrate entries and applying a modest 10-15 minute prebolus for known meals to reduce afternoon postprandial peaks.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: In the absence of logged carb entries, the loop relies entirely on UAM detection. Afternoon glucose elevations indicate that waiting for UAM triggers alone results in delayed insulin delivery, while late-night dipping highlights the risk of stacking unannounced tail insulin.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Record carbohydrate entries and meal timestamps over a 7-day period to evaluate postprandial response curves and validate active carb ratios.

exceptions.pattern: Fast-absorbing or liquid meals / unexpected early acceleration
exceptions.suggestion: Rely on UAM high boost and dynamic ISF without adding manual boluses to avoid stacking on top of unrecorded intake.
exceptions.rationale: Prevents over-correction when meal composition is variable or unannounced.

exceptions.suggestion: Ensure temporary targets or proactive correction microdosing are permitted if pre-meal announcements are missed.
exceptions.rationale: Mitigates postprandial afternoon hyperglycemia peaks without altering baseline basal rates.

implementation_steps: Step 1: Review current glucose metrics, time in range (86.0%), and hypoglycemia frequency (5.1%) with the care team.
Step 2: Maintain all current AAPS profile settings, basal rates, ISF, CR, and automation parameters unchanged.
Step 3: Begin logging carbohydrate entries consistently for all meals over the next 7 to 14 days.
Step 4: Monitor postprandial glucose excursions and re-evaluate profile carb ratios once meal-linked data is available.
